subject: Segmentation & custody expectations — hosted vs dedicated vs VPC (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@fintegrity.com>, Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@fintegrity.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Segmentation & custody expectations — hosted vs dedicated vs VPC (post-call recap)

Hi Marta / Ethan —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we don’t lose momentum. High-level notes from our conversation:

- Primary constraint: Fintegrity will process PHI and requires tenant separation such that no other customer workloads share the same compute hosts or storage namespaces.
- Crypto: customer-managed keys (BYOK) are preferred for data-at-rest; strong audit trail for key usage is required.
- Control plane residency: legal team asked about control-plane metadata (user ids, audit logs) and whether it can live in a customer VPC / dedicated control plane.
- Network: strict inbound/outbound egress rules, optional private peering, and explicit support for IP allowlists are expected.
- Evidence: SOC 2 attestation and a topology diagram are needed for procurement.

What we proposed on the call (summary):
- Hosted API: easiest to get started but does not meet your single-tenant compute requirement for PHI workloads.
- Dedicated capacity: single-tenant GPU pools (reserved capacity) with tenant-level data separation and configurable egress; can be provisioned in a shared control plane but isolated compute.
- Private VPC / on-prem: full customer VPC option; optional private control plane and BYOK via your KMS/HSM; highest isolation and auditability.

Attachments: I’m attaching a short segmentation summary and our SOC2 stub to start the compliance review.

Requested from you:
1) Please confirm the minimal evidence your procurement needs (topology diagram? SOC2 report copy? Data flow statement?).
2) Confirm whether the requirement is strictly "no shared compute hosts" or if a cryptographically isolated multi-tenant host would be acceptable.
3) If you prefer, we can schedule a separate 30-minute security deep-dive with engineering and your infosec team.

Next internal owners / timeline:
- I’ll coordinate a short security call and deliver a topology diagram within 3 business days.
- Marissa will follow up on licensing/pricing for Dedicated vs Private options.
- Karthik — please prepare a high-level note on BYOK (HSM integration) and control-plane residency limitations for the proposed options.

Proposed next meeting: Thu, Aug 20 — 10:00am PT. Is that OK on your end?

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: redwood-segmentation-summary.pdf; SOC2-Type2-Attestation-Stub.pdf

From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@fintegrity.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@fintegrity.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Segmentation & custody expectations — hosted vs dedicated vs VPC (post-call recap)

Thanks, Irene — helpful recap. A few clarifications inline: 

> - Primary constraint: Fintegrity will process PHI and requires tenant separation such that no other customer workloads share the same compute hosts or storage namespaces.

Correct — the procurement ask is "single-tenant compute" for PHI processing (no co-located customer workloads on the same hosts).

> - Crypto: customer-managed keys (BYOK) are preferred for data-at-rest; strong audit trail for key usage is required.

Yes, BYOK is required for E2E data-at-rest. We will also expect logging of key usage events and the ability to rotate keys on our schedule.

Two questions:
1) For Dedicated capacity, can you confirm whether the GPU hosts are truly dedicated (single-tenant) or if there is any host multiplexing at the hypervisor / container layer? We need a short statement we can put in the procurement RA.
2) For Private VPC, do you offer an option where the control plane telemetry (audit logs, user identities) is pushed into our GCP project/account (we prefer logs to be retained in our environment)?

Attaching our compliance checklist; I highlighted items we need answered for procurement. Ethan will drive the procurement side and loop in legal if needed.

— Marta
Marta Lopez
Head of Security & Privacy, Fintegrity
marta.lopez@fintegrity.com
Attachments: Fintegrity-Compliance-Checklist.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 15:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Segmentation & custody expectations — suggested answers for Marta

Irene — quick draft replies you can copy into a response to Marta: 

- Dedicated capacity: Redwood provisions single-tenant GPU pools for Dedicated customers. Hosts are not shared with other customers at the hypervisor level; we run a tenant-bound cluster topology that guarantees single-tenant allocation for the committed pool. (We can provide a short statement for procurement.)

- BYOK: Supported on Private VPC by default (customer KMS/HSM). For Dedicated we support customer-managed keys integrated via our KMS proxy/HSM connectors in many configurations — note: for the strictest control plane residency the Private VPC option is recommended.

- Audit logs & control-plane telemetry: We can stream audit logs to your GCP project or S3 bucket for retention; for Private VPC we can optionally deploy a control-plane component that keeps metadata inside your environment.

- Next step: offer a 2-week mini-POC on a Dedicated pool scoped to PHI workloads (single-tenant), or run a Private VPC trial if you need control-plane residency from day one.

I’ll draft the procurement statement and the topology diagram. Want me to take the call with Fintegrity next week?

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@fintegrity.com>, Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@fintegrity.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Segmentation & custody expectations — hosted vs dedicated vs VPC (post-call recap)

Marta / Ethan —

Thanks for the checklist and the clarification. Below are concise answers you can share internally; I’ve attached the short procurement-ready statement and a one-page topology.

1) Dedicated capacity — statement for procurement: 
Redwood Inference Dedicated capacity is provisioned as single-tenant GPU pools. Hosts in the committed pool are not shared with other customers at the hypervisor or OS level. Network and storage namespaces are isolated per tenant; we can provide an attestation statement for contract binding. (See attached PDF: redwood-segmentation-summary.pdf)

2) BYOK and key usage logging — short note: 
- Private VPC: full BYOK/HSM integration available; keys remain under your account; key operations can be logged to your audit sinks.
- Dedicated: customer-managed keys supported via our KMS connector; key usage events are logged and can be exported to your logging destination. For the highest operational control we recommend Private VPC.

3) Control-plane telemetry
We support log export (Stackdriver/GCP, CloudWatch, S3) for audit logs. For Private VPC we can optionally deploy a control-plane proxy so metadata and identities remain in your environment.

4) Evidence and artifacts
We attached: SOC2-Type2-Attestation-Stub.pdf (summary) and a topology diagram link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3cSegmentationDiagram. If you need the full SOC2 report we can provide it under an NDA.

5) Next steps / proposed schedule
- 30-min security deep dive (engineering + infosec): Thu, Aug 20 — 10:00am PT (proposed).
- Procurement statement & topology PDF delivered (attached).
- Option: 2-week Dedicated mini-POC scoped to PHI processing (we can scope infra and sample SLA).

Please confirm the meeting time and whether you want us to proceed with the Dedicated mini-POC scoping exercise or move straight to Private VPC documentation.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: redwood-segmentation-summary.pdf; SOC2-Type2-Attestation-Stub.pdf
